title: Affine nilpotent preparation over the reduced integral base
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with $T$ irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components], generic point $\xi$ [def-sc-generic-point], and nonreduced scheme-theoretic fibre $X_\xi$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Put $i:T'=T_{\mathrm{red}}\to T$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction] and $X'=X\times_T T'$ [def-pc-base-change]. Then $T'$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], $i$ is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces, and the projection $X'\to T'$ is of finite type. For each $t'\in T'$ with image $t\in T$, the residue-field map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(t')$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism and the projection induces a canonical isomorphism $X'_{t'}\cong X_t$ over these fields. There exist a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T'$ containing its generic point $\xi'$, an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X'\times_{T'}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $b\in B$, $n\geq1$, such that $A$ is a domain, $B$ is a finite type $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], $b^n=0$, and $b\otimes1\ne0$ in $B\otimes_A K$ [def-weil-module-base-change], where $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)=\kappa(\xi')$ is the localization of $A$ at its zero prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Moreover, for every $a\in A$, the further restriction $V_a=D(a)=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ has $U\times_VV_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ as an affine open of $X'\times_{T'}V_a$, compatibly with the structure maps; here subscripts denote localization [def-weil-ring-localization-away].

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, proof from reduction of the base through the second shrinking making h nilpotent

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-reduction-universal-homeomorphism] to $T$: $i:T_{\mathrm{red}}\to T$ is a homeomorphism and $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ is reduced. The homeomorphism carries irreducibility and the generic point to $T'$; explicitly $\overline{\{\xi'\}}=T'$. Thus $T'$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Apply clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] to $f$ and $i$ to obtain that $f':X'\to T'$ is finite type.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, first proof paragraph; Tags 054M, 01ON, 01T4

proof.text: For $t'\in T'$, the map $\kappa(t)\to\kappa(t')$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso], since the reduction map is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-of-base-change], $X'_{t'}=X_t\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t')$ with its projection to $X_t$. Since the field map is invertible, the inverse field map and the identity of $X_t$ give the inverse to that projection by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. This proves the claimed canonical comparison, including at $\xi'$, where it preserves the nonreducedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0575, first proof paragraph: reduction identifies fibres

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ of $\xi'$ using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Integrality gives that $A_0$ is a domain [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Its generic point is $(0)$ and its stalk there is its fraction field $K$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field]; the residue field of this field is itself [def-weil-residue-field]. The generic fibre of $Y_0=X'\times_{T'}V_0$ is the fibre from step 2: the inverse maps are given by the same projection pairs in the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. This family is finite type by clause (2) of [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change].

source.place: Tag 0575, first paragraph: replace the integral base by an affine open

proof.text: The nonreduced generic fibre has a point $x$ with nonreduced local ring, by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Its image $y\in Y_0$ has an affine neighbourhood $U_0=\operatorname{Spec}B_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. The map $A_0\to B_0$ is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-chart-base-change-iso] to $Y_0\to V_0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}K\to V_0$ with these charts: the inverse image of $U_0$ in the generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_{A_0}B_0)$, with its projection induced by $b\mapsto1\otimes b$. It contains $x$. Its local ring at $x$ is a prime localization of its coordinate ring by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. If this coordinate ring were reduced, that local ring would be reduced by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-preserves-reduced], a contradiction. Therefore it contains a nonzero nilpotent $h$, with $h^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$. Tensor symmetry identifies this ring with $B_0\otimes_{A_0}K$: the maps $k\otimes c\mapsto c\otimes k$ and $c\otimes k\mapsto k\otimes c$ are inverse by the balancing relations, and respect multiplication on pure tensors.

source.place: Tag 0575, proof: pick an affine open and a nonzero nilpotent generic section; Tags 01T2, 01JR, 01I4, 01HV

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $B_0\otimes_{A_0}K$ is the localization of $B_0$ at the images of $A_0\setminus\{0\}$. Write $h=c/s$, with $c\in B_0$ and $s\in A_0$ nonzero. The equation $h^n=0$ says that $c^n/1=0$, so the zero criterion in that cited statement gives $u\in A_0\setminus\{0\}$ with $u c^n=0$ in $B_0$. Set $g=su\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $V=D(g)\subseteq V_0$ is affine with ring $A=(A_0)_g$; it contains $(0)=\xi'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], $U=U_0\times_{V_0}V$ is an affine open of $X'\times_{T'}V$ with ring $B_0\otimes_{A_0}A=B=(B_0)_g$, the last equality again by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. These comparisons respect both projections.

source.place: Tag 0575, the two shrinkings making the generic section a nilpotent section; Tags 00DK, 01HV, 01I3, 01JR, 01I4

proof.text: In $B=(B_0)_g$ both $s$ and $u$ are units: their inverses are respectively $u/g$ and $s/g$. Put $b=c/s$. Then $b^n=c^n/s^n=0$, since $u c^n=0$ and $u$ is invertible. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-ring-localization-universal-property] identifies the fraction field of $A=(A_0)_g$ with $K$: all nonzero fractions from $A_0$ become invertible in $K$, and conversely $A_0\subset A$ gives the inverse map between the two fraction fields. Their maps are inverse because they agree on the numerators and inverses. The same universal property identifies $B\otimes_AK$ with $B_0\otimes_{A_0}K$: both are the ring obtained from $B_0$ by inverting every nonzero element of $A_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change]. Under this comparison $b\otimes1=h\ne0$. The nonempty affine open $V$ of the integral scheme $T'$ has domain ring $A$ [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Finally $B$ is finite type over $A$: if $c_1,\ldots,c_r$ generate $B_0$ over $A_0$, their images generate $(B_0)_g$ over $(A_0)_g$, as each fraction $P(c_1,\ldots,c_r)/g^e$ is the same polynomial with coefficients in $(A_0)_g$.

source.place: Tag 0575, second shrinking; explicit localization arithmetic

proof.text: Let now $a\in A$, including $a=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime], $V_a=D(a)=\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ as an open subscheme with the localization structure map. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] to the open $U$ and this base restriction: $U\times_V V_a$ is open in $X'\times_{T'}V_a$ with its natural projections. The affine fibre-product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] and localization base change [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change] identify it with $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A A_a)=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$, respecting both structure maps. This is the final compatibility assertion.
